intended_object: The density of the Gompertz distribution with shape η > 0 and scale b > 0: f(x) = η b e^{bx} e^{η} exp(−η e^{bx}) for x ≥ 0, and 0 otherwise. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body is η·b·exp(bx)·exp(−η(exp(bx) − 1)). This is the standard Gompertz density η b e^{bx} e^{η} e^{−η e^{bx}}, just written in a different order. The definition gives 0 when x ≤ 0. The textbook support is x ≥ 0, so the two differ only at the single point x = 0. That point has Lebesgue measure zero, so the distribution is the same. When the parameters are not positive the definition also gives 0. This is a junk-value choice, as the docstring says, and the usual convention. The construction is for a real-valued density, so ℝ is the natural setting. I searched Mathlib's source for "gompertz" (ignoring case) and found nothing, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
